{{Short description|British physicist}}
'''George Raymond "Ray" Satchler''' (14 June 1926, London, UK – 28 March 2010, [[Shelton, Washington]], U.S.) was a British-American nuclear physicist.

==Biography==
After serving from 1944 to 1948 the [[Royal Air Force]], Satchler studied at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref name=Sentinel>{{cite news|title=Obituary. George Raymond "Ray" Satchler|newspaper=Knoxville News Sentinel|date=April 7, 2010|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/knoxnews/name/george-satchler-obituary?id=11054227}}</ref> where he graduated in 1951 with a B.A. and an M.A.<ref name=AIP>{{cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11609004.html |title=G. R. Satchler. Biography |website=Physics History Network, American Institute of Physics (AIP)}}</ref> and in 1955 with a doctorate in physics. His thesis advisor was John Ashley Spiers.<ref name=PT/> As a postdoc Satchler was from 1956 to 1957 a research associate at the [[University of Michigan]] and from 1956 to 1959 a research fellow at [[Imperial Chemical Industries]].<ref name=AIP/> He was a physicist at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]], from 1959 to 1996, when he retired.<ref name=Sentinel/><ref name=PT>{{cite journal |title=Obituary of George Raymond Satchler |author=Ball, James B.|author2=Bertrand, Fred E.|author3=Galindo-Uribarri, Alfredo|author4=McGrory, Joseph B.|journal=Physics Today|date=October 2010|doi=10.1063/PT.4.1886|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/PT.4.1886/full/|url-access=subscription}} (This obituary erroneously states that Satchler was named a Fellow of the APS in 1976 — the correct year is 1961.)</ref> From 1994 to 2005 he was a professor at the [[University of Tennessee]].<ref name=AIP/> He was the author or co-author of over 275 papers.<ref name=PT/>

Satchler was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS) in 1961.<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1961&unit_id=&institution=Oak+Ridge+National+Laboratory}} (Search on year "1961" and institution "Oak Ridge National Laboratory".)</ref> In 1976 he was named a Corporate Fellow of Oak Ridge National Laboratory,<ref>{{cite web|title=Corporate Fellow G. Raymond Satchler (1976)|website=Oak Ridge National Laboratory|url=https://www.ornl.gov/our-people/g-satchler}}</ref> which at that time was operated by the [[Union Carbide Corporation]] under a contract with the U.S. federal government.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Timeline (pages ii–vi)|journal=Oak Ridge National Laboratory Review|volume=25|issue=3 & 4|year=1992|url=https://www.ornl.gov/sites/default/files/ORNL%20Review%20v25n3-4%201992.pdf}}</ref> In 1977 he received, jointly with [[Stuart Thomas Butler]], the [[Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics]] for "their discovery that direct nuclear reactions can be used to determine angular momenta of discreet nuclear states and for their systematic exploitation of this discovery permitting the determination of spins, parities and quantitative properties of nuclear wave functions."<ref>{{cite web|title=1977 Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics Recipient, G. Raymond Satchler|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Satchler&first_nm=G&year=1977}}</ref>

In Yorkshire in 1948 Satchler married Margaret Patricia "Pat" Enid Gibson. Upon his death he was survived by two daughters and a grandson.<ref name=Sentinel/>
